rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah continued constructing the ship until the command came, while his people mocked him.
rows.anchor: bu gayeye gelinceye kadar Nûh gemi sun‘una devam eyliyor, kavmi de alay ediyordu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tennur means an enclosed oven or furnace, most commonly called a tandır in Turkish.
rows.anchor: “Tennûr” lügatta kapalı bir ocak, bir fırındır ki lisânımızda en ziyade “tandır” tâbir olunur.

rows.speaker: Leys
rows.claim: Leys says tennur is a word that passed into every language and gives tennar as its companion form.
rows.anchor: Leys demiştir ki: “Tennur umûmiyetle her lisâna geçmiş bir lafızdır. Arkadaşı ‘tennâr’dır”

rows.speaker: Ezherî
rows.claim: Ezherî argues that tennur was foreign but became Arabic through Arabization.
rows.anchor: Ezherî de demiştir ki: “Bu delâlet eder ki isim bazen a‘cemî olur, Arap onu ta‘rîb eder de Arabî olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Feveran means boiling or gushing with force and intensity.
rows.anchor: “Feverân” da mâlumdur ki kuvvet ve şiddetle kaynamak, fışkırmaktır.

rows.speaker: most exegetes
rows.claim: Most exegetes agree that tennur has its literal meaning of an oven.
rows.anchor: Ekser müfessirîn “tennûr”un hakikaten bir ocak mânasına olduğunda müttefiktir.

rows.speaker: some exegetes
rows.claim: Some identify the oven as one belonging specifically to Noah; many call it a bread oven.
rows.anchor: Kimisi Nûh’a mahsus bir tennur idi demiş. Birçoğu ekmek pişirilen bir fırın idi demiş

rows.speaker: some exegetes
rows.claim: Among the reported origins are an oven left from Adam and one where Noah’s wife baked bread.
rows.anchor: bunu da kimi Âdem’den kalma idi demiş, kimi Hazret-i Nûh’un zevcesinin ekmek pişirdiği bir tennur idi demiş

rows.speaker: some exegetes
rows.claim: Reports place the oven at Kufa’s mosque site, in Damascus near Ayn Vardan, or in India; one report says it was stone.
rows.anchor: Kimi taştan idi, kimi Kûfe tarafında idi demiş ve hatta Hazret-i Ali’den Kûfe mescidinin yerinde idi diye bir söz nakledilmiş.

rows.speaker: some exegetes
rows.claim: Other reports locate the oven in Damascus at Ayn Vardan or in India.
rows.anchor: Kimi Şam’da “Ayni verdan” nâm mevzide, kimi de Hind’de idi demiş

rows.speaker: some exegetes
rows.claim: These literal-oven reports explain the boiling as water bubbling and spurting from the oven like water in a cauldron.
rows.anchor: bütün bunlar “feverân”ı suyun kazanda kaynar gibi fırından kaynayıp fışkırmasıyla îzah etmişlerdir.

rows.speaker: some exegetes
rows.claim: They say God had announced the flood’s onset to Noah and made the eruption a sign to begin loading.
rows.anchor: bu alâmet ve mucize zuhur ettiği zaman yüklemek emrini vermiş demişler.

rows.speaker: some exegetes
rows.claim: Since tennur can mean earth, this interpretation takes its boiling as waters bursting from the ground, as described in al-Qamar.
rows.anchor: Arabda bazen yeryüzüne de “tennur” ıtlâkı vâki‘olduğundan tennûrun feverânı yeryüzünden suların fışkırması olacak.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the earth-as-furnace idea is noteworthy, boiling in this reading would more fittingly mean fire erupting, not water.
rows.anchor: bu surette feverâna yakışan mâna su fışkırması değil, ateş püskürmesi olurdu.

rows.speaker: some exegetes
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes tennur as the earth’s honored, elevated places, where water erupted as a miracle.
rows.anchor: Tennur”dan murad, arzın şerefli ve yüksek mevzileri demektir ki bir hârika olarak oralara bile sular fışkırmıştır demişler.

rows.speaker: Hazret-i Ali
rows.claim: A report attributed to Ali interprets the phrase as dawn breaking or morning coming.
rows.anchor: fâra’t-tennûr” şafak attı, sabah oldu mânasına gelir denilmiş ve bunun Hazret-i Ali’den menkul olduğu söylenmiş.

rows.speaker: some exegetes
rows.claim: Some understand the phrase metaphorically as matters heating up or intensifying, like the idiom “the oven heated.”
rows.anchor: İş kızıştı, şiddetlendi mânasına حَمِيَ الْوَطِيس “fırın kızdı” denildiği gibi “fâra’t-tennûr” da böyledir denilmiş.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority see no reason to abandon the literal sense of tennur for these four metaphorical readings.
rows.anchor: cumhûr-ı müfessirîn “tennur” kelimesinin hakīkī mânasından udûle sebep olmadığını söylemektedirler.

rows.speaker: Hasan
rows.claim: Hasan is reported by Abu Hayyan as defining tennur as the place where water collects in the ship.
rows.anchor: Ebû Hayyân tefsîrinde Hasan’dan rivayet olarak “tennur”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A literal oven and a shipboard basin or boiler where water gathers are compatible; the majority’s oven report does not conflict with Hasan’s report.
rows.anchor: ocak olması aynı zamanda onun gemide su toplanan bir kazan ile müterâfık olmasına mâni‘değildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in al-tennur points to an oven belonging to the ship, which could also be Noah’s special miraculous oven.
rows.anchor: “Lâm-i ahd” ile “et-tennûr” buyurulması bunun gemiye ait bir tennur olmasında zâhirdir.

rows.speaker: Sâhib-i Keşşâf
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf says hatta attaches to the earlier verb for making the ship, so the sense is “he made the ship until.”
rows.anchor: Sâhib-i Keşşâf’ın da tasrîhi vechile âyette حَتَّىٰ gayesi yukarıdaki يَصْنَعُ fiiline müte‘allik olup mâna يَصْنَعُ الْفُلْكَ حَت َّى demek olduğu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this syntax, the oven’s boiling marks the completion of the ship’s construction and the start of loading and movement; the ship’s engine is firing up.
rows.anchor: nihâyet emrimiz gelip gemi fayrab edildiği vakit

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is clear in its literal and apparent meaning, so there is no reason to seek a figurative reinterpretation.
rows.anchor: nasta hakikati ve zâhiri bırakıp da tevil aramaya hiç de sebep yoktur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection that such a steamship could not have been made then, or that its craft would not have been forgotten, is only incredulity.
rows.anchor: o zaman öyle bir vapur nasıl yapılabilirdi ve yapılmış olsa bu sanat unutulur mu idi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: History contains examples of practical technologies once known and later lost, so forgotten shipbuilding knowledge is no decisive objection.
rows.anchor: mukaddemâ mâlum olup da sonradan gāib olmuş sanâyi‘-i tecrîbiyenin bile tarihte misâli eksik olmadığı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ship was made under God’s care and revelation, according to the earlier command in this sura.
rows.anchor: ber vech-i bâlâ وَٱصْنَعِ ٱلْفُلْكَ بِأَعْيُنِنَا وَوَحْيِنَا mantûkunca Allah teâlâ’nın hıfz u vahyi ile yapılmış olan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cargo included male-female pairs of every kind, though God alone knows its full particulars.
rows.anchor: erkeği dişisi bulunan her şeyden -ki tafsîlini Allah bilir- ikişer tane humûle alabilen

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ship also carried Noah’s household except one son and a small number of believers from his people.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Nûh’un bir oğlundan başka ehl ü iyâlini ve az miktarda da olsa kavminden iman etmiş olanları dahi yüklenerek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A miraculous vessel carrying this cargo through waves like mountains is less implausible as a steamship than as an ordinary sailing boat.
rows.anchor: dağlar gibi dalgalar içinde cereyan edip giden hârikulâde bir geminin alelâde bir yelken gemisi farz edilmesi daha müsteb‘ad olacağında şüphe edilemez.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh’s command, government, or work is not a sound order likely to end well.
rows.anchor: Firavun kumandası veya Firavun işi ve hükûmeti, sonu iyi gelecek musîb bir emir değildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naming Pharaoh again where a pronoun could stand is meaningful: the first mention concerns Pharaoh himself, the second his characteristic.
rows.anchor: Zira evvelkinde Firavun’un şahsı, ikincide de[^2] vasfı kast olunmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first phrase means Pharaoh’s own order; the second generalizes to the order of Pharaoh’s faction.
rows.anchor: evvelkisi bilhassa Firavun’un emri demek olduğu hâlde ikincisi umûmiyetle Firavun emri, yani Firavun kısmının emri demektir.

rows.speaker: Ebû Hayyân
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says Pharaoh denied a creator and afterlife and taught that each land’s people must obey its ruler, leaving his command wholly without right guidance.
rows.anchor: Ebû Hayyân tefsîrinde der ki: “Firavun sâni‘i ve me‘âdı münkir bir dehrî idi ve diyordu ki ‘âlemin ilâhı yoktur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh claimed to be the supreme lord, recognizing no lord above himself.
rows.anchor: Ve’n-Nâzi‘ât Sûresi’nde geleceği üzere Firavun أَنَا۠ رَبُّكُمُ ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh issued commands by personal desire without testing them against truth or God’s commands, treating himself as absolute sovereign.
rows.anchor: mücerred kendi nokta-i nazarına, kendi temâyülât ve iradesine göre emir veriyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The laws governing creation and human destiny cannot be changed by one person’s or a group’s will; Pharaoh’s absolutism falsely tries to redefine good and evil and harms ruler and subjects alike.
rows.anchor: emr ü iradesi ile değişmeyeceği âşikârdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Judgment Day Pharaoh leads his people to the fire as if to water; water cools and quenches thirst, whereas fire does the opposite, making it a dreadful destination.
rows.anchor: Çünkü suya harâret söndürmek, ciğer soğutmak için gidilir, ateş ise bunun zıddı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people’s fate is heart-rending because they ignored Moses and followed Pharaoh’s order, whose outcome was evil.
rows.anchor: Mûsâ’ya bakmadılar da âkıbeti böyle fena olan bir Firavun emrine ittibâ‘ettiler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For following Pharaoh, his people were continually pursued by a curse in this world and will be cursed on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: hem bu dünyada hem de kıyamet gününde bir lânet metbû‘u kılındılar Firavun’a teba‘iyetlerinin cezâ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rifd is something added to another thing for support, such as felt under a saddle, assistance given, or a gift.
rows.anchor: Rifd” aslında dayansın diye bir başkasına izâfe edilen şeydir. Mesela eğerin ve semerin altına vurulan keçe, birine yapılan i‘âne, verilen atıyye rifddir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling hellfire a vird and the curse a rifd is an eloquent sarcastic metaphor.
rows.anchor: cehenneme “vird”, lânete “rifd” tâbir olunması tehekküm için gayet beliğ bir istiaredir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rifd may mean a bad aid, with the curse as the ill assistance given to Pharaoh’s followers.
rows.anchor: Ne fena rifddir bu[^4] merfud ne kötü i‘ânedir bu yapılan i‘âne, yani lânet.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, rifd is a bad gift: the curse bestowed as the reward for being Pharaoh’s followers.
rows.anchor: Veya ne kötü câizedir bu câize, yani Firavun tebaası olmanın bahşişi olan bu lânet bahşişi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Accounts of the messengers are recounted to strengthen the Prophet’s heart; this sura brings truth, admonition, and reminder for believers.
rows.anchor: peygamberlere müte‘allik ehemmiyetli haberlerden- kalbini onunla tesbit edeceğimiz her türlüsünü naklediyoruz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers are told to act according to their capacity; all their power is devoted to disbelief.
rows.anchor: “hâlinize, kuvvetinize göre yapacağınızı yapın” yani sizin bütün gücünüz imansızlığa yetiyor.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers will work by affirming the truth and accepting their Lord’s admonition and warning in faith.
rows.anchor: her hâlde biz âmiliz hakkı tasdik ve Rabbimizden gelen va‘z u ihtârı kabul ederek iman ile çalışacağız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelievers are to keep awaiting a calamity for believers, while believers await God’s promises and a similarly bad end for the faithless.
rows.anchor: yani Rabbimizin vaadlerini ve sizin gibi imansızların başlarına gelen kötü âkıbetlere benzer bir âkıbetinizi iman ile gözlemekteyiz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unseen of the heavens and earth belongs to God; only He knows and brings forth what is not yet present.
rows.anchor: yoktur ki O’na dayanmadan hakkında bir hüküm verilmek mümkin olabilsin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone knows all universals and particulars, nonexistent and existent things, and what is present or unseen; nothing is hidden from Him.
rows.anchor: Bütün külliyyât ve cüz’iyyâtı, ma‘dûmât ve mevcûdâtı, hâzırları ve gāibleri bilen ancak O’dur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every matter returns to God; no judgment about anything in the seen or unseen is possible independently of Him, even the claim that two times two is four.
rows.anchor: Kulluğunu yap, emrini tut, öyle mütevekkil ol

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet must worship God and entrust matters to Him; reliance without worship is of no use, so one should obey as a servant.
rows.anchor: ibadetsiz tevekkülün de fâidesi yoktur. Kulluğunu yap, emrini tut, öyle mütevekkil ol

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing of Hud strongly confirms the ending of Bara’a and prepares for the following sura, Yusuf.
rows.anchor: Sûre-i Hûd’un bu hâtimesiyle Sûre-i Berâe’nin hâtimesine beliğ bir teyid ve bundan sonra gelecek olan Sûre-i Yûsuf’a da bir temhid yapılmıştır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbelievers demand another sign despite the many signs and miracles already given; fixed disbelief keeps them from accepting proof, and they seek a coercive miracle.
rows.anchor: Sana indirilen bunca âyetlere, mucizelere inanmaz, küfrederler. Küfür, tomruk gibi boyunlarına geçmiş bulunduğu için onları nübüvvetine kâfî delil saymazlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s task toward them is warning, not bringing glad tidings or guiding them to faith.
rows.anchor: Sen onları tebşir edecek veya halkı hidâyetle yola getirecek değilsin. Bunlar hakkında vazifen inzardan ibarettir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is a guide for every people, while God is the one who creates guidance.
rows.anchor: Allah hidâyeti halkeden O’dur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows what every female carries, whether human, animal, or plant, including its source, lawful or unlawful origin, sex, future, life, and spiritual outcome.
rows.anchor: Hangi tohumdan? Helâlden midir, haramdan mıdır?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows what wombs diminish or increase, including what they absorb, expend, add, impair, or complete in the developing child.
rows.anchor: Aldığı alûkta ne tahlil yapar? Ne maddeler tarh eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His knowledge also covers gestational duration and timing, whether birth is early or late and before, at, or after stages of formation.
rows.anchor: Vakti er mi geç mi oluyor? Veledin hilkati belirmeden mi, belirdikten sonra mı? Hamlin ekall-i müddetinde mi, ekser-i müddetinde mi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He knows whether a birth yields one child, two, or more.
rows.anchor: Sâlisen aded itibariyle bir mi, iki veya daha ziyade mi olur?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Birth variations are not random errors; they occur under God’s knowledge, opposing naturalism and showing divine will and life-science knowledge.
rows.anchor: Bunlar tabiat davası aleyhine irade delîli olduğu gibi, aynı zamanda ilme de müsteniddir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every thing is measured and bounded in its beginning, end, stage, time, and particular state; the causal chain rests on God and nothing escapes His knowledge.
rows.anchor: Her şeyin merâtib-i tekvinde tecavüz edemeyeceği muayyen bir haddi, bir vakti bir hâl-i mahsûsu vardır ve bütün silsile-i esbâb Allah’a dayanır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For God, the actualization of anything at any stage of existence, or its potentiality, is presential knowledge.
rows.anchor: Her şeyin nefsü’l-emirde herhangi bir mertebe-i vücudda tahakkuku veya ona isti‘dâdı Allah teâlâ’ya nisbetle bir ilm-i huzûrîdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows both the unseen and the witnessed, or the nonexistent and the existent.
rows.anchor: O, gayba ve şehadete de âlim Allah, hislerden gāib olanı da bilir, hâzır olanı da. Veyahut ma‘dûmu da mevcûdu da bilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God knows the unseen and the witnessed, He knows whether sign-seekers want guidance or are acting from obstinacy.
rows.anchor: âyet isteyenlerin hidâyet için mi, inad için mi ne gibi bir maksadla istediklerini de bilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kabir means supremely great, with everything beneath God and nothing capable of encompassing Him; Muta‘ali means exalted in power and transcendent above created limits.
rows.anchor: Kebîr yani her şey kendisinin dûnunda olan ve hiçbir vechile kābil-i ihâta olmayan yegâne büyük

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance belongs to God, and nothing lies outside His knowledge, power, or presence.
rows.anchor: Onun için hidâyet O’na aittir. Ve O’nun ilm ü kudretinden hâriç kalacak ve huzûr u likāsına çıkmayacak hiçbir şey yoktur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Secret speech and public speech, hiding by night and moving openly by day are all equally known to God.
rows.anchor: içinizden sözünü gizleyen küfrü gönlünde söyleyen

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each person has pursuing attendants before and behind who record speech and action, or continually protect that person.
rows.anchor: onu hıfz ederler her birinin sözünü ve fiilini zabt eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The attendants are under God’s command, understood as spirits or angels in line with the phrase in al-Isra.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın emrinden ibaret birtakım ervâh veya melâikedirler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since everyone’s words and actions are watched and protected by God, hidden and public deeds cannot go without recompense.
rows.anchor: O hâlde hepsi mahfuz olan ve hepsi tâkip olunmakta bulunan gizli veya açık akvâl veya ef‘âliniz cezâsız kalır mı?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not change a people’s state, including blessing, prosperity, or any good or bad condition, until they change what is within themselves; responsibility accords with their free choice.
rows.anchor: Yani bir müddet için iradelerinde serbesttirler ve mes’ûliyetleri iradeleriyle mütenâsibdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same principle appears in al-Anfal: God does not change a blessing bestowed on a people until they change themselves.
rows.anchor: Sûre-i Enfâl’de ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَمْ يَكُ مُغَيِّرًۭا نِّعْمَةً أَنْعَمَهَا عَلَى قَوْمٍ حَتَّىٰ يُغَيِّرُوا۟ مَا بِأَنفُسِهِمْ âyetine bak [8/53].

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When God wills harm for a people, it cannot be averted; it occurs as He wills, whether temporarily or permanently.
rows.anchor: İsteseler de istemeseler de o Allah’ın murad ettiği vechile muvakkatse muvakkaten, müebbedse müebbeden vâki‘olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They have no protector or governor besides God who could avert that harm.
rows.anchor: yoktur ki reddine çare bulsun.
